reviews.quote: This compact tablet continues to be nearly unrivaled. Pros: fast SoC, optional lots of memory, Pencil and 5G possible, PWM-free display, compact. Cons: stale display-to-surface ratio, refresh rate only 60 Hz, no high-res audio via Bluetooth, only 12 months warranty.

praises: 293g one-handed tablet that reads books, comics, and PDFs better than anything bigger — the form factor has no real rival (r/ipad)
A17 Pro with hardware ray tracing runs AAA console ports (Resident Evil Village, Death Stranding) on a pocket tablet
Fully laminated 8.3" display — pen and touch feel flush, unlike the non-laminated base iPad
8GB RAM + Apple Intelligence means it is fully current on AI features despite the clearance price
USB 3 10Gb/s USB-C drives external SSDs and mirrors to monitors — pro-grade I/O in the smallest iPad
complaints: No official keyboard of any kind — no Smart Connector, so laptop-style typing needs a third-party Bluetooth case that crowds the 8.3" screen
8.3" is cramped for Stage Manager / split-screen two-app work — the productivity pitch is thin
60Hz 500-nit LCD at mini pricing; no OLED or ProMotion anywhere in the mini line
Touch ID in the top button is awkward one-handed; no Face ID
128GB fills fast once you install a couple of ray-traced AAA games (15GB+ each)

design_philosophy: The only serious small tablet: Apple's bet that a 293g, fully-laminated, desktop-class-silicon slate beats 'bigger is better' for reading, travel, gaming, and one-handed use. The 2024 A17 Pro generation added Apple Intelligence and console-grade GPU to that formula; the deliberate omission is any keyboard path — the mini is a content and gaming tablet, not a laptop substitute.
